name: Guardian cryptic crossword, Penguin book 2 No 14

book.title: The New Penguin Book of The Guardian Crosswords, volume 2

clue.text: Risk cats' meat used by motorist in a spot

definitions.text: used by motorist in a spot

blocks.note: a hazard is a risk or danger
lights are animal lungs, traditionally sold as cheap food for cats

explanation.surface: Someone takes a chance on feeding pet food to a driver stuck in a tight corner.
explanation.walkthrough: Lights, the lungs of slaughtered animals, were the classic cats' meat sold by street vendors in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver stopped awkwardly switches on the flashing warning indicators so other traffic knows to steer round the car.

clue.text: Demolition job telling hen what to do with egg?

definitions.note: a hatchet job is a demolition job; the second word of the phrase stands in the clue

indicators.note: telling means speaking the instruction out, so the clue word is heard rather than read

blocks.clueFragment: hen what to do with egg?
blocks.note: a hen's job with an egg is to hatch it

explanation.surface: Someone gives a broody hen instructions about her egg, oddly called a demolition job.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, 'hatch it' is the axe word; the definition leans on the phrase hatchet job, a savage destructive attack or review.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatchet job is a vicious critical attack that tears a person or work apart, so the axe word fits a demolition.

clue.text: Policeman with poem follows last one on American mail

indicators.note: follows puts the policeman and poem after what comes next in the clue, so the order is swapped

blocks.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet
the Roman numeral for one
Police Constable
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A constable carrying verse trails the final item in a delivery of American post.
explanation.walkthrough: The postal code in the United States is written on every envelope there; Britain calls it a postcode.
explanation.definitionFit: Every address on letters sent within the United States carries this numeric postal routing number.

clue.text: Searches for remains in dissolute man's bowling

blocks.note: a rake is a dissolute, pleasure-seeking man
in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end

explanation.surface: Someone sifts the leftovers from a libertine's game of bowls.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a cricket term: six deliveries bowled in a row by one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: To rake over ashes or old ground is to sift through what is left looking for something.

clue.text: Weapon followed by lot?

blocks.note: surface reading: an arm that a whole crowd comes after
setter's reading: put the word lot after this weapon and you get a knight of the Round Table

explanation.walkthrough: Lot here is not a crowd but three letters to tack on: the weapon plus lot names Arthur's knight Sir Lancelot.
explanation.definitionFit: A long pointed spear carried by a mounted knight is the weapon, and it begins the famous knight's name.

clue.text: Fuel supplier makes profit with small Scottish entry

indicators.note: an entry is a going in, so the small Scottish word goes inside the profit

blocks.note: a gain is a profit
sma' is Scots for small

explanation.surface: A fuel company turns a profit through a minor deal north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: Sma' is the Scots form of small, familiar from Burns.
explanation.definitionFit: The large underground pipe carrying gas to a street's houses is what supplies their fuel.

clue.text: Ends winter without success with small car

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letters for success are taken out of winter

blocks.note: taken as written
a win is a success
the Mini is a famous small British car

explanation.surface: A cold season of failure finishes with a little car.
explanation.definitionFit: Termini are end points, the plural of terminus, so they are the ends of lines or routes.

clue.text: European way to pay (say) with European capital on short holiday (say)

indicators.note: say asks you to speak the way to pay, keeping the sound and changing the spelling
short marks an abbreviation, so the holiday word is a clipped form

blocks.note: a cheque is a way of paying
the capital of Norway
vac is short for vacation

explanation.surface: A traveller settles a bill in a European city during a brief break.
explanation.walkthrough: Both '(say)' markers work: CHEQUE is respelt and VAC, the British short form of vacation, is respelt with a K.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the former Czechoslovakia is a European nationality, now split into Czech and Slovak.

clue.text: 8 7 dn runner changed at Oz for Chinese city, in short

definitions.note: a runner from the country at 7 down

indicators.note: changed means rearranged, so these letters are put in a new order
in short means cut down, so the city's name loses its ending

blocks.note: taken as written
the old spelling of Beijing

explanation.surface: A runner swaps an Australian start for a Chinese city.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray 8 is the clue's own number; Emil Zatopek, the 7-down runner, won three golds at the 1952 Olympics.
explanation.definitionFit: Emil Zatopek was a Czechoslovak long-distance runner, one of the greatest athletes of his era.

clue.text: No way to drink quack medicine

blocks.note: taken as written
St is short for street, a way
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to swallow a charlatan's remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To drink' looks like a verb phrase, but drink is just the noun rum.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a patent remedy of dubious effectiveness, the kind peddled by a charlatan.

clue.text: Silencer internally attached to note on piano by compiler?

definitions.note: this setter's pseudonym Araucaria is the monkey puzzle tree

indicators.note: internally means on the inside, so the following words go inside the silencer

blocks.note: a muzzle stops a dog barking or biting
attached is on, and a note is a key
p is the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: A muzzle gets fitted inside, with something on the piano by a puzzle setter.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter Araucaria took his name from Araucaria araucana, the monkey puzzle tree, so a puzzle by this compiler is literally one.
explanation.definitionFit: Araucaria, this crossword's setter, is the Latin name of the spiky South American conifer.

clue.text: Accountant laughs at collusion

blocks.note: Chartered Accountant
hoots are loud laughs

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper laughs at a crooked arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in cahoots is to be in secret partnership, conspiring together for some shady purpose.

clue.text: Number one story returns in ecstasy

indicators.note: returns means comes back, so the string is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: No. is the abbreviation for number
the Roman numeral for one
a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A chart-topping tale comes back in rapture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one' reads as a chart-topper, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is a state of great happiness and exhilaration, close in sense to ecstasy.

clue.text: Exotic engineers on strike?

blocks.note: workers on strike are out
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Engineers downing tools would be something unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers (RE) is a British Army corps; the pieces go in the reverse of clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré means unconventional or bizarre, beyond the ordinary, which matches strange and exotic.

clue.text: Saint has a time of fasting in a fruit tree .. .

indicators.note: in places the fasting period inside the fruit plant

blocks.note: a vine bears grapes
taken as written
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: A holy man spends the fasting season up a fruit tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into 16 across, which finishes the thought.
explanation.definitionFit: St Valentine is the martyr whose feast on 14 February is celebrated by lovers.

clue.text: Despair or become enamoured?

blocks.note: first meaning: to become discouraged
second meaning: to lose one's heart to someone, falling in love

explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase means opposite moods: losing courage, or losing one's heart to a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing heart is giving up hope, while losing your heart to someone is falling in love with them.

clue.text: ... used by devil's little brother when fluttering

definitions.note: with 14 across: the ones who use a valentine

indicators.note: fluttering means flapping about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
bro is a short form of brother

explanation.surface: Following on, a valentine is sent by a demon's kid brother, all aflutter.
explanation.walkthrough: Read with 14 across: a valentine is used by courting couples, the answer here.
explanation.definitionFit: Courting couples are called lovebirds, and they are the people who send each other valentine cards.

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for six
tri- is the prefix for three
zero looks like the letter O
the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A string of numbers poses as a chemistry formula, like a lab label for a strong acid.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray 17 is the clue's own number; the scan has lost the 0 and the subscripts of the formula.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil of vitriol is the old name for sulphuric acid, whose chemical formula this is.

clue.text: Composer has a lot of European capital with little weight

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the capital loses its last letter

blocks.note: the capital of Germany
oz is the abbreviation for ounce, a small weight

explanation.surface: A composer owns much of a European city, though he is light on his feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Hector Berlioz was a French Romantic composer, best known for the Symphonie fantastique.

clue.text: Distressed, reduced and increased

blocks.note: cut means reduced, as with prices
up means raised, increased

explanation.surface: Something is upset, made smaller and made bigger, all at once.
explanation.walkthrough: Opposite meanings side by side make the clue look contradictory; each just gives one word.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cut up about something is British slang for being very upset or grief-stricken.

clue.text: Conservative leader has first-class row with base fellow

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of the party name
A1 means first-class, with the 1 read as I
a tiff is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: A Tory leader has a top-notch quarrel with a low-life.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is a common grading for first-rate, and the digit stands in for I.
explanation.definitionFit: A caitiff is an archaic word for a contemptible coward or villain, a base wretch.

clue.text: They include strike in treatment

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it within, so the pronoun wraps around the blow

blocks.note: taken as written
to rap is to strike sharply

explanation.surface: Some people make room for industrial action in a course of care.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is the medical or psychological treatment of an illness or disorder.

clue.text: Surgeon, English, fled from old soldier

blocks.note: a vet is an animal surgeon
E is the abbreviation for English
ran is the past tense of run, to flee

explanation.surface: An English doctor ran away from an ex-serviceman.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran is someone with long service, especially a former member of the armed forces.

clue.text: Nose around, for example, in the Middle East

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the nose word wraps the example abbreviation

blocks.note: neb is a dialect word for a beak or nose
e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Someone pokes about, say, out in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nose around' looks like a verb, to snoop, but nose is the noun and around wraps it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Negeb, or Negev, is the desert region of southern Israel, so it lies in that part of the world.

clue.text: The fez I made for a fiddler

indicators.note: made means fashioned, so these letters are put together into something new

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hatmaker boasts of crafting a fez for a violinist.
explanation.definitionFit: Jascha Heifetz was a celebrated Lithuanian-born American violinist; fiddler is a casual word for violinist.

clue.text: Grievous bodily harm done by Pole if held by monarch

indicators.note: held by means gripped from outside, so the ruler goes around the two pieces

blocks.note: a king is a monarch
N is the North Pole
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Polish man inflicts serious injury, if a king allows it.
explanation.walkthrough: Pole looks like a nationality, but it is one end of the earth's axis, N or S.
explanation.definitionFit: A knifing is a stabbing attack, a clear case of serious bodily injury inflicted on someone.

clue.text: David's maid gets a large beer, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the drink is listened to rather than spelt

blocks.note: taken as written
big means large
ale is beer

explanation.surface: A servant of King David is treated to a pint of something strong.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible Abigail called herself David's handmaid before marrying him; abigail also came to mean a lady's maid.
explanation.definitionFit: Abigail, wife of King David, described herself as his handmaid, and the name later meant any lady's maid.

clue.text: Reformer gets queen to cook

blocks.note: Elizabeth is the name of English queens
to fry is to cook in fat

explanation.surface: A campaigner for change gets the monarch to make dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Elizabeth Fry was a Quaker prison reformer, once pictured on the Bank of England five-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth Fry campaigned in nineteenth-century England for humane treatment of prisoners, a famous social reformer.
